code: library(myceliumr) data(example_cohort)

title: Getting Started with myceliumr
text: Study object describes overall research project:
code: study <- study_new(   study_id = "STUDY001",   title = "My Genomics Project",   description = "Comparing rat and mouse expression",   hypotheses = "Orthologs show conserved patterns",   aims = "Map regulatory regions",   assays = c("WES", "snRNA-seq"),   genome_builds = list(rat = "rn6", mouse = "mm10") )  study #> <myceliumr::Study> #>  @ study_id     : chr "STUDY001" #>  @ title        : chr "My Genomics Project" #>  @ description  : chr "Comparing rat and mouse expression" #>  @ hypotheses   : chr "Orthologs show conserved patterns" #>  @ aims         : chr "Map regulatory regions" #>  @ assays       : chr [1:2] "WES" "snRNA-seq" #>  @ genome_builds:List of 2 #>  .. $ rat  : chr "rn6" #>  .. $ mouse: chr "mm10" #>  @ created_at   : POSIXct[1:1], format: "2026-02-05 05:33:28" #>  @ tags         : chr(0)

title: Getting Started with myceliumr
text: Individual subjects (animals samples): Supported species: rat, mouse, human.
code: subject1 <- subject_new(   subject_id = "RAT001",   species = "rat",   sex = "M",   strain = "Lewis",   genotype = "WT" )  subject1 #> <myceliumr::Subject> #>  @ subject_id: chr "RAT001" #>  @ species   : chr "rat" #>  @ sex       : chr "M" #>  @ strain    : chr "Lewis" #>  @ genotype  : chr "WT" #>  @ cohort    : chr NA #>  @ timepoint : chr NA #>  @ notes     : chr NA

title: Getting Started with myceliumr
text: manifest CSV defines subjects sample mappings. Required columns: subject_id - unique identifier species - rat, mouse, human Optional columns: sex, strain, genotype, cohort, timepoint, notes, assay IDs like assay_wes_id, assay_snrna_id. Example: load CSV:
code: manifest <- tibble::tribble(   ~subject_id, ~species, ~sex, ~strain, ~genotype, ~cohort, ~assay_wes_id,   "RAT001", "rat", "M", "Lewis", "WT", "Control", "WES_R001",   "RAT002", "rat", "F", "Lewis", "WT", "Control", "WES_R002",   "MOUSE001", "mouse", "M", "C57BL/6", "WT", "Control", "WES_M001",   "MOUSE002", "mouse", "F", "C57BL/6", "KO", "Treatment", "WES_M002" )  manifest #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   subject_id species sex   strain  genotype cohort    assay_wes_id #>   <chr>      <chr>   <chr> <chr>   <chr>    <chr>     <chr>        #> 1 RAT001     rat     M     Lewis   WT       Control   WES_R001     #> 2 RAT002     rat     F     Lewis   WT       Control   WES_R002     #> 3 MOUSE001   mouse   M     C57BL/6 WT       Control   WES_M001     #> 4 MOUSE002   mouse   F     C57BL/6 KO       Treatment WES_M002 manifest <- read_manifest_csv("path/to/manifest.csv")

title: Getting Started with myceliumr
text: Cohort combines Study validated subject data:
code: # First validate the manifest manifest_split <- validate_manifest(manifest)  # Create cohort from validated components cohort <- cohort_new(   study = study,   subject_tbl = manifest_split$subject_tbl,   sample_map = manifest_split$sample_map )  cohort #> <myceliumr::Cohort> #>  @ study      : <myceliumr::Study> #>  .. @ study_id     : chr "STUDY001" #>  .. @ title        : chr "My Genomics Project" #>  .. @ description  : chr "Comparing rat and mouse expression" #>  .. @ hypotheses   : chr "Orthologs show conserved patterns" #>  .. @ aims         : chr "Map regulatory regions" #>  .. @ assays       : chr [1:2] "WES" "snRNA-seq" #>  .. @ genome_builds:List of 2 #>  .. .. $ rat  : chr "rn6" #>  .. .. $ mouse: chr "mm10" #>  .. @ created_at   : POSIXct[1:1], format: "2026-02-05 05:33:28" #>  .. @ tags         : chr(0)  #>  @ subject_tbl: tibble [4 × 6] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame) #>  $ subject_id: chr [1:4] "RAT001" "RAT002" "MOUSE001" "MOUSE002" #>  $ species   : chr [1:4] "rat" "rat" "mouse" "mouse" #>  $ genotype  : chr [1:4] "WT" "WT" "WT" "KO" #>  $ sex       : chr [1:4] "M" "F" "M" "F" #>  $ strain    : chr [1:4] "Lewis" "Lewis" "C57BL/6" "C57BL/6" #>  $ cohort    : chr [1:4] "Control" "Control" "Control" "Treatment" #>  @ sample_map : tibble [4 × 2] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame) #>  $ subject_id  : chr [1:4] "RAT001" "RAT002" "MOUSE001" "MOUSE002" #>  $ assay_wes_id: chr [1:4] "WES_R001" "WES_R002" "WES_M001" "WES_M002" #>  @ paths      : list() #>  @ analyses   : list()

title: Getting Started with myceliumr
text: Get subject table: Get sample mapping:
code: subjects <- cohort@subject_tbl subjects #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   subject_id species genotype sex   strain  cohort    #>   <chr>      <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>   <chr>     #> 1 RAT001     rat     WT       M     Lewis   Control   #> 2 RAT002     rat     WT       F     Lewis   Control   #> 3 MOUSE001   mouse   WT       M     C57BL/6 Control   #> 4 MOUSE002   mouse   KO       F     C57BL/6 Treatment samples <- cohort@sample_map samples #> # A tibble: 4 × 2 #>   subject_id assay_wes_id #>   <chr>      <chr>        #> 1 RAT001     WES_R001     #> 2 RAT002     WES_R002     #> 3 MOUSE001   WES_M001     #> 4 MOUSE002   WES_M002

title: Getting Started with myceliumr
text: Validation happens automatically object creation. Invalid data raises clear error messages:
code: # This will fail - invalid species bad_subject <- subject_new(   subject_id = "BAD001",   species = "zebra fish"  # Error: not rat/mouse/human )  # This will fail - missing required columns bad_manifest <- tibble::tibble(subject_id = c("S1", "S2")) cohort_bad <- cohort_new(   study = study,   subject_tbl = bad_manifest,   sample_map = tibble::tibble() ) # Error: species column is required

title: Getting Started with myceliumr
text: Use built-example cohort explore:
code: data(example_cohort)  # View the study example_cohort@study #> <myceliumr::Study> #>  @ study_id     : chr "STUDY001" #>  @ title        : chr "Cross-species genomics comparison" #>  @ description  : chr "Example study comparing rat and mouse genomes" #>  @ hypotheses   : chr [1:2] "Orthologous genes show conserved expression patterns" ... #>  @ aims         : chr [1:2] "Map rat genes to mouse orthologs" ... #>  @ assays       : chr [1:2] "WES" "snRNA-seq" #>  @ genome_builds:List of 3 #>  .. $ rat  : chr "rn6" #>  .. $ mouse: chr "mm10" #>  .. $ human: chr "hg38" #>  @ created_at   : POSIXct[1:1], format: "2026-02-05 04:16:44" #>  @ tags         : chr(0)  # View subjects example_cohort@subject_tbl #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   subject_id species genotype sex   strain  cohort    timepoint #>   <chr>      <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>   <chr>     <chr>     #> 1 RAT001     rat     WT       M     Lewis   Control   Day0      #> 2 RAT002     rat     WT       F     Lewis   Control   Day0      #> 3 MOUSE001   mouse   WT       M     C57BL/6 Control   Day0      #> 4 MOUSE002   mouse   KO       F     C57BL/6 Treatment Day0  # View samples example_cohort@sample_map #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>   subject_id assay_wes_id assay_snrna_id #>   <chr>      <chr>        <chr>          #> 1 RAT001     WES_R001     SNRNA_R001     #> 2 RAT002     WES_R002     SNRNA_R002     #> 3 MOUSE001   WES_M001     SNRNA_M001     #> 4 MOUSE002   WES_M002     SNRNA_M002

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: immutable S7 class managing cross-species cohort data. Cohorts combine validated subject-level metadata sample--assay mappings optional study context, file paths, analysis results. primary data container WES snRNA-seq analyses across rat, mouse, human studies.

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
code: Cohort(   study = NULL,   subject_tbl = structure(list(), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"), row.names =     integer(0), names = character(0)),   sample_map = structure(list(), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"), row.names =     integer(0), names = character(0)),   paths = list(),   analyses = list() )

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: study Study object providing project-level context metadata, NULL applicable. Optional. subject_tbl tibble (data frame) containing subject-level metadata. Required columns: subject_id (character), species (rat/mouse/human). Optional columns: sex, strain, genotype, cohort, timepoint, notes. Validated validate_cohort(). sample_map tibble mapping subjects assay-specific sample IDs. Must include subject_id column referential integrity. Additional columns typically include assay_wes_id, assay_snrna_id, etc. Validated validate_cohort(). paths Named list file paths data files results directories. Optional, defaults empty list. analyses Named list containing analysis results, intermediate tables, data objects later retrieval. Optional, defaults empty list.

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: Use cohort_new() construct Cohort objects comprehensive validation. Validation ensures: Required columns subject_tbl sample_map Valid species values (rat/mouse/human) Referential integrity subject_tbl sample_map duplicate subject IDs Access properties via @ operator:
code: cohort@study       # Study object or NULL cohort@subject_tbl # Subject metadata table cohort@sample_map  # Sample mapping table cohort@paths       # File paths cohort@analyses    # Stored analysis results

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: immutable S7 class storing research project metadata cross-species genomics studies. Study objects provide high-level context configuration cohorts analyses involving rat, mouse, human subjects.

title: S7 Study class — Study
code: Study(   study_id = character(0),   title = character(0),   description = NA_character_,   hypotheses = character(0),   aims = character(0),   assays = character(0),   genome_builds = list(),   created_at = structure(1770266595.37765, class = c("POSIXct", "POSIXt")),   tags = character(0) )

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: study_id Character scalar study identifier. Unique within project. title Character scalar study name/title. description Character scalar longer description study purpose, design, protocols. Optional. hypotheses Character vector research hypotheses. Optional. aims Character vector specific research aims. Optional. assays Character vector assay types used (e.g., "WES", "snRNA-seq"). Optional. genome_builds Named list mapping species genome build versions (e.g., list(rat = "rn6", mouse = "mm10", human = "hg38")). Optional. created_at POSIXct timestamp creation. Defaults current time. tags Character vector arbitrary tags categorization. Optional.

title: S7 Study class — Study

code: study@study_id study@title study@description study@hypotheses study@aims study@assays study@genome_builds study@created_at study@tags

Optional. genotype Character scalar genetic background modification (e.g., "WT", "KO"). Optional. cohort Character scalar cohort membership treatment group. title: Create a Cohort object — cohort_new
text: subject_tbl tibble containing subject-level metadata. Required columns: subject_id (character) species (rat/mouse/human). Optional columns: sex, strain, genotype, cohort, timepoint, notes. Typically obtained validate_manifest(). sample_map tibble mapping subjects assay-specific sample IDs. Must least subject_id column link subject_tbl. Additional columns can include assay_wes_id, assay_snrna_id, etc. Typically obtained validate_manifest(). study Study object providing project-level metadata context, NULL applicable. Defaults NULL. paths Named list file paths data files results directories. Optional defaults empty list. analyses Named list containing analysis results intermediate data objects later retrieval. Optional defaults empty list.

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: Reads CSV file containing cross-species subject metadata sample mappings, validates structures data subject sample tables suitable creating Cohort object. primary entry point loading external manifest data.

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
code: read_manifest_csv(path, ...)

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: path Character scalar file path CSV manifest file. Path must exist file must readable. ... Additional named arguments passed readr::read_csv(), col_types, skip, comment, etc.

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: list two elements: subject_tbl: Tibble containing subject-level metadata (subject_id, species, sex, strain, genotype, cohort, timepoint, notes) sample_map: Tibble mapping subjects assay-specific sample IDs

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: manifest CSV must contain least two columns: subject_id: Unique identifier subject (character) species: Species designation - one "rat", "mouse", "human" (character) Optional subject metadata columns automatically detected: sex: Biological sex strain: Strain breed designation genotype: Genetic background modification cohort: Treatment group cohort membership timepoint: Study timepoint collection date notes: Free-form notes additional columns treated sample/assay IDs placed returned sample_map. Typical assay columns include: assay_wes_id: WES sample identifier assay_snrna_id: snRNA-seq sample identifier

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
code: # Create a temporary CSV manifest manifest_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") writeLines(   "subject_id,species,sex,strain,assay_wes_id\n    RAT001,rat,M,Lewis,WES_R001\n    MOUSE001,mouse,F,C57BL/6,WES_M001",   manifest_file )  # Read and validate the manifest manifest_split <- read_manifest_csv(manifest_file) print(manifest_split$subject_tbl) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   subject_id species sex   strain  #>   <chr>      <chr>   <chr> <chr>   #> 1 RAT001     rat     M     Lewis   #> 2 MOUSE001   mouse   F     C57BL/6 print(manifest_split$sample_map) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   subject_id assay_wes_id #>   <chr>      <chr>        #> 1 RAT001     WES_R001     #> 2 MOUSE001   WES_M001

text: Subject objects S7 classes storing individual-level metadata cross-species studies. Species validation ensures compatibility across supported organisms (rat, mouse, human). Individual subjects typically grouped Cohort objects collective analysis.

title: Create a Subject object — subject_new
code: # Create a rat subject rat_subject <- subject_new(   subject_id = "RAT001",   species = "rat",   sex = "M",   strain = "Lewis",   genotype = "WT",   cohort = "Control" ) print(rat_subject) #> <myceliumr::Subject> #>  @ subject_id: chr "RAT001" #>  @ species   : chr "rat" #>  @ sex       : chr "M" #>  @ strain    : chr "Lewis" #>  @ genotype  : chr "WT" #>  @ cohort    : chr "Control" #>  @ timepoint : chr NA #>  @ notes     : chr NA  # Create a mouse subject mouse_subject <- subject_new(   subject_id = "MOUSE001",   species = "mouse",   sex = "F",   strain = "C57BL/6",   genotype = "KO" ) print(mouse_subject) #> <myceliumr::Subject> #>  @ subject_id: chr "MOUSE001" #>  @ species   : chr "mouse" #>  @ sex       : chr "F" #>  @ strain    : chr "C57BL/6" #>  @ genotype  : chr "KO" #>  @ cohort    : chr NA #>  @ timepoint : chr NA #>  @ notes     : chr NA

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: Ensures Cohort object satisfies structural integrity requirements cross-species genomics analysis. Validates subject table, sample map, referential integrity . Intended internal validation step called automatically cohort_new().

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
code: validate_cohort(x)

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: x S7 object expected Cohort class instance.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: Invisibly returns TRUE validation succeeds. Throws informative errors validation fails.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: VALIDATION CHECKS: x actually Cohort object subject_tbl sample_map data frames subject_tbl includes required columns: subject_id, species sample_map includes subject_id column subject_id species character vectors, non-empty duplicate subject_id values subject_tbl species values valid (rat/mouse/human) Referential integrity: sample_map$subject_id values exist subject_tbl Validation performed automatically cohort_new(), can called directly debugging custom Cohort construction.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
code: # Create valid cohort components subjects <- data.frame(   subject_id = "RAT001",   species = "rat",   sex = "M" ) samples <- data.frame(   subject_id = "RAT001",   assay_wes_id = "WES_R001" ) cohort <- cohort_new(   subject_tbl = subjects,   sample_map = samples )  # Validation succeeds (called automatically above) validate_cohort(cohort)

title: Validate and structure a manifest table — validate_manifest
text: Validates manifest data frame tibble containing cross-species subject metadata sample identifiers. Automaticallyr structures data subject-level sample-level tables suitable Cohort construction. Comprehensive validation ensures data integrity compatibility.

title: Validate and structure a manifest table — validate_manifest
code: validate_manifest(manifest)

title: Validate and structure a manifest table — validate_manifest
text: manifest data.frame tibble subject metadata optional sample/assay ID columns. See Details required optional columns.

title: Validate and structure a manifest table — validate_manifest
text: list two elements: subject_tbl: Tibble subject-level metadata sample_map: Tibble subject--sample mappings

title: Validate and structure a manifest table — validate_manifest
text: REQUIRED COLUMNS: subject_id (character): Unique subject identifier, duplicates allowed species (character): Species designation - one "rat", "mouse", "human" (case-insensitive) RECOGNIZED OPTIONAL SUBJECT COLUMNS (placed subject_tbl): sex: Biological sex strain: Strain/breed designation genotype: Genetic background modification cohort: Treatment group cohort assignment timepoint: Study timepoint collection date notes: Free-form annotations SAMPLE ID COLUMNS (placed sample_map): additional columns listed treated assay-specific sample identifiers included sample map. Examples: assay_wes_id: WES sample identifier assay_snrna_id: snRNA-seq sample identifier VALIDATION CHECKS: required columns present non-empty subject_id species character vectors missing empty values required columns duplicate subject_id values species values valid (rat/mouse/human)

title: Validate and structure a manifest table — validate_manifest
code: # Create valid manifest manifest <- data.frame(   subject_id = c("RAT001", "RAT002", "MOUSE001"),   species = c("rat", "rat", "mouse"),   sex = c("M", "F", "M"),   strain = c("Lewis", "Lewis", "C57BL/6"),   genotype = c("WT", "WT", "KO"),   assay_wes_id = c("WES_R001", "WES_R002", "WES_M001") )  # Validate and structure result <- validate_manifest(manifest) print(result$subject_tbl) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   subject_id species genotype sex   strain  #>   <chr>      <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>   #> 1 RAT001     rat     WT       M     Lewis   #> 2 RAT002     rat     WT       F     Lewis   #> 3 MOUSE001   mouse   KO       M     C57BL/6 print(result$sample_map) #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   subject_id assay_wes_id #>   <chr>      <chr>        #> 1 RAT001     WES_R001     #> 2 RAT002     WES_R002     #> 3 MOUSE001   WES_M001
